title: Stephen R. Jordan, Editor

sections.h: Editor of The World of AI
sections.body:
Stephen R. Jordan edits The World of AI. He spent three decades in enterprise security, operations and risk, including product security incident response at Intel and McAfee and global endpoint security at Citi, and is the author of the nine volume Operating Discipline for AI Library™.

He is the founder of SRJ Consulting & Services LLC, the Frisco, Texas company that publishes the site. He decides what the site tracks, which sources it trusts and the rules its software follows. He checks what that software produces by sampling it and acting on reader reports, and is responsible for everything published here. How that works in practice is set out in the editorial policy.

The sections of this site follow the work he has actually done.

  • AI CVE tracker. He spent nearly four years in product security incident response, first as a PSIRT engineer at Intel, then as team lead of McAfee's Product and Application Security Incident Response Team, where CVE assignment and publication to MITRE ran inside McAfee's CVE Numbering Authority. The AI CVE tracker applies that discipline to AI products.
  • AI law and compliance frameworks. He holds a master's degree in political science, and Volume III of his book series maps AI governance controls to eleven regulatory and standards frameworks, including the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and SR 11-7.
  • AI Insurance. He spent nearly ten years running a commercial insurance brokerage with offices in Plano and Shanghai, owning its accounting, regulatory filings and risk transference work.

Jordan began at McAfee in 1995 as its first antivirus consultant, building the deployment and remediation practice and leading implementations for clients including Citibank, the New York Stock Exchange and Boeing. He went on to manage McAfee's systems engineering team for IT security sales, earning President's Club recognition three times.

From 2005 to 2014 he ran Jordan and Jordan Insurance Group, a commercial brokerage he co founded, with offices in Plano and Shanghai and a fifteen person team in China.

He then returned to security. At Intel, from 2014 to 2017, he handled inbound vulnerability reports as a product security incident response engineer, owning reproduction, severity scoring and remediation coordination. At McAfee, from 2017 to 2018, he led the global Product and Application Security Incident Response Team, directing six lead engineers and 120 senior security architects, running coordinated disclosure with outside researchers and governing the Security Development Lifecycle.

At Citi he owned Level 3 endpoint security across roughly 500,000 endpoints in 165 countries. At Optiv, one of the largest pure play security advisories in North America, he scoped multiyear enterprise engagements with chief information, executive and data officers. He founded SRJ Consulting & Services in 2023.

He holds a Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting and a Master of Arts in Political Science, with a minor in business statistics, from West Texas A&M University. He completed 102 graduate credit hours of doctoral coursework in curriculum and instruction at East Texas A&M University, with concentrations in computer science and educational media and technology.

Jordan is the author of The Operating Discipline for AI Library™, a nine volume series on running artificial intelligence as a managed business function. All nine volumes were published between May and September 2026, totaling more than 3,200 pages, by SRJ Consulting & Services Publishing, in hardcover, paperback and Kindle. Most volumes carry Library of Congress and Dewey Decimal classifications.

He is also the author of The AI Lawyer, a novel, published in August 2026.

Where a page on this site draws on one of his books, the page says so.

SRJ Consulting & Services sells advisory work on AI governance, risk and security. It sells no software and holds no vendor partnerships. Jordan co-owned and ran Jordan & Jordan Insurance Group from 2005 to 2014 and no longer holds any interest in it; the AI Insurance section of this site draws on that former brokerage experience and says so. No commercial relationship changes a ranking, a legal status, a case summary or a verdict on this site. The disclosure page sets out what is paid.

To report an error or reach the editor, write to theworldofai@inkboxmail.com or use the contact page, and name the page. Confirmed errors are corrected on the page itself, as described under Data Quality and Corrections.
